title: 40% Upfront. 64% Drip-Fed.
caption:
Writing a longer spec made the agent worse, not better.

Tencent and CUHK ran 61 tasks from 34 repos through 12 frontier models, every one of them on Claude Code. Whole spec upfront: 40.3% finished. Same requirements fed in stages, with the user reporting bugs: 64.1%. Identical tasks, identical acceptance tests.

My admission: I've been writing three-page PRDs before letting Claude Code touch anything, convinced I was saving myself turns. The turns were the point.

Spec first or stages?

slides.sub: Same 61 tasks. Same acceptance tests. Only the delivery changed. FeatureLoop, Oct 26.

slides.title: 12 Models. One Harness.
slides.sub: 61 tasks, 34 repos, 2,196 runs. Every model ran inside Claude Code, so the harness was never the variable.

slides.title: Three Ways To Ask
items: Fed in order as work proceeds: 51.6%

slides.headline:
You Report It.
It Stays Broken.
slides.sub: Only 15.4% of failed stages came fully right within two revisions. And 20.9% of fixes left another requirement unmet.

slides.headline:
It Checked
A Stub Instead
slides.sub: In 75.3% of failed runs the agent skipped the real user path, or validated a helper, stub or proxy in its place.
